summary: Reads DMX universe data from a DMX Out POP or DMX Fixture POP and outputs a table for visualizing layouts and debugging channel conflicts.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Continuously grab current DMX universe data when enabled

key_params.name: updateval
key_params.note: Update the value column with the latest channel values while enabled

key_params.name: updatevalpulse
key_params.note: Grab the latest value update on demand

key_params.name: dmxpop
key_params.note: DMX Fixture POP or DMX Out POP to inspect

key_params.name: netfilter
key_params.note: Pattern filter for DMX net values

key_params.name: subnetfilter
key_params.note: Pattern filter for DMX subnet values

key_params.name: universefilter
key_params.note: Pattern filter for DMX universe values

key_params.name: netaddressfilter
key_params.note: Pattern filter for combined network address values

key_params.name: excludeunused
key_params.note: Hide unused channels instead of listing all 512 channels per universe

key_params.name: extension
key_params.note: Edit/view file extension exposed to external editors

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when Extension is set to Custom Extension

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Common DAT node-display word wrap setting

common_gotchas: DMX Map DAT depends on POP-based DMX operators and is not a standalone DMX input/output node.
Leaving Exclude Unused Channels off can create large tables because every universe contains 512 channels.
When Update Value is off, values can be stale until a universe rearrangement or manual pulse occurs.
Use filters before driving UI tables from large rigs, otherwise the DAT can become noisy and expensive to scan.
key_concepts: Reads a DMX Out POP or DMX Fixture POP and outputs a table of mapped DMX channels.
Network, subnet, universe, and net-address filters constrain which DMX rows appear.
Update parameters control when the table refreshes from the source DMX POP arrangement.
Exclude Unused hides unmapped fixture channels when a compact map is desired.
